faq.q: What is the difference between a hold and a tap?
faq.a: Holding the input produces a longer, higher arc that clears wider gaps. Tapping produces a short hop for narrow gaps. The entire skill ceiling of the game lives inside knowing when to hold and when to tap.

faq.q: Why do I keep dying at pattern transitions?
faq.a: The gap pattern shifts every ten platforms — long stretches reward held inputs, short stretches reward tapping. Deaths most commonly occur on the first platform of a new pattern because players carry the previous rhythm into the wrong gap size. Read the new pattern before reacting.

faq.q: What is an edge landing?
faq.a: Landing as close to the leading edge of a platform as possible awards a style bonus on top of your score. Edge landings also leave a longer jump window for the next leap, making them both higher-scoring and tactically safer.

faq.q: Where should I look — at my feet or ahead?
faq.a: Keep your eyes one platform ahead of where you are standing, not on the platform you are leaving. Looking at your current position causes late jumps; looking ahead lets you commit to the right input before landing.

faq.q: What do I do when the scrolling gets impossibly fast?
faq.a: Switch from reacting to predicting. At extreme scroll speeds, the gap pattern is the only usable signal. Commit to the platform rhythm rather than tracking individual visuals — trust the physics and let your muscle memory drive the timing.

featuredComments.text: Edge landings are simultaneously the highest-scoring play and the safest next-jump setup. The game is telling you the optimal strategy is also the risky-looking one. Once that clicks, your scores jump immediately.

featuredComments.name: RhythmLeap

featuredComments.name: MuscleTrust

featuredComments.name: AheadOfFeet
featuredComments.text: Look one platform ahead of where you are standing, not at your current position. I was told this three times before it stuck. Then it immediately improved my average run by 40 platforms.

22.title: Mythic Defender: Heroes Returns v2.0
22.description: A card-driven tower defense where mythic heroes return to hold the line against endless legions.
22.fullDescription:
Mythic Defender: Heroes Returns fuses classic tower defense with deck-building strategy. Draw heroes from your card pool, place them along the path, and unleash devastating abilities to crush waves of orcs, demons, and worse.
      Every map is a puzzle of positioning and timing. Some heroes deal heavy single-target damage, others rain area-of-effect lightning, and a few support the whole line with auras. Mix and match to counter what each wave throws at you.
      Earn mana between rounds, upgrade your strongest heroes, and unlock new cards as you progress deeper into the campaign. The legions never stop — how long can your kingdom stand?
22.controls: Mouse: Drag hero cards onto valid tiles, click heroes to upgrade or activate abilities, click UI buttons to start waves and manage your deck.
22.tips: Front-load tanky melee heroes near chokepoints to soak damage while ranged casters work safely from the back. Save mana for the wave's elite enemies — burning everything early leaves you defenseless when the boss arrives. Upgrades scale better than placing more low-tier units; concentrate your firepower.
22.lore:
Once, the Mythic Heroes walked among mortals — Thor of the Storm Hammer, the rune-bound shieldmaidens of the North, the silent archers of the Whispering Wood. When the world found peace, they faded into legend, their cards sealed in the vaults of forgotten kings.
      Now the Burning Horde has torn through the seals, and ancient citadels burn beneath blood-red skies. The cards have begun to glow again. The heroes are returning — but only one defender can summon them.
      You hold the deck. The legions are at the gate.
features: Diverse Hero Roster with Unique Abilities

faq.q: How does the card summoning system work?
faq.a: You draw hero cards from your deck at the start of each round. Drag cards onto valid tiles along the enemy path to summon them. Heroes remain on the map until they are defeated or the round ends.

faq.q: Where should I place melee heroes?
faq.a: Front-load tanky melee heroes near chokepoints to absorb damage while ranged casters work safely from the back row. A melee hero positioned deep into the map near your core provides no damage reduction for the path before it.

faq.q: When should I save mana instead of spending it?
faq.a: Save mana for each wave's elite enemies and boss arrivals. Burning all mana on standard enemies leaves you defenseless when the boss appears — bosses require concentrated upgraded firepower, not distributed low-tier units.

faq.q: Is it better to upgrade one hero or place more?
faq.a: Upgrades scale better than placing additional low-tier units. Concentrate your mana on your strongest frontline hero rather than spreading upgrades evenly — a single well-upgraded hero outperforms three under-upgraded ones.

faq.q: What is the Burning Horde?
faq.a: The Burning Horde is the army that has torn through the ancient seals and set citadels ablaze. It consists of orcs, demons, and worse — each wave is a new portion of the Horde pressing toward your position.

23.title: Falling Dodger
23.description: A neon free-fall arcade run — twist through saw blades, lasers, and lightning while distance and obstacle count climb together.
23.fullDescription:
Falling Dodger drops you into an endless neon shaft where gravity does the driving. Your only job is to steer — slide left and right between spinning saw blades, pulsing lasers, and arcs of electric current as the shaft scrolls past faster and faster.
      Two numbers define your run: total distance fallen and total obstacles cleared. Distance is the primary score, but the leaderboard uses obstacle count as the tiebreaker — so threading the tightest gaps is always worth more than playing it safe.
      The deeper you fall, the more aggressive the patterns get. Twin saws close from both walls. Laser grids force last-second commits. Lightning chains punish hesitation. Every meter is earned.
      One mistake ends the run. How far can you fall?
23.controls: Keyboard: A / D or ←/→ to steer. Touch: tap or drag left/right side of the screen.
23.tips: Stay centered between threats — committing to a wall early leaves you no escape when the next pattern shifts. Read two obstacles ahead, not one; the shaft scrolls faster than your reactions at high speed. Tight gaps reward more obstacle points than wide ones, so push for the narrow line when distance is close.
23.lore:
Deep beneath the synthwave city lies the Shaft — an infinite neon tunnel said to drill through reality itself. Each night, runners jack in and fall, chasing the legend of what waits at the bottom.
      No one has ever found it. The shaft keeps growing, the obstacles keep evolving, and the names on the leaderboard keep climbing. Every meter is a vote against gravity.
23.objectives: Steer through an endless neon shaft, dodging spinning saw blades, pulsing lasers, and lightning arcs as long as possible — maximizing total distance fallen as your primary score and obstacle count as the tiebreaker on the global leaderboard.

faq.q: How is my score calculated?
faq.a: Distance fallen is your primary score. Total obstacles cleared is the tiebreaker on the leaderboard — threading tight gaps always adds more obstacle points than wide ones, so pushing through narrow passages is worth the risk when distance scores are close.

faq.q: What are the three hazard types?
faq.a: Spinning saw blades, pulsing lasers, and lightning arcs. Each has different timing — saws spin at fixed speeds, lasers pulse in intervals, and lightning chains punish hesitation. Learning each hazard's rhythm lets you commit earlier and thread tighter gaps.

faq.q: Where should I position myself in the shaft?
faq.a: Stay centered between threats. Committing to a wall early leaves no escape when the next pattern shifts. Center positioning maximizes your available reaction directions as patterns change.

faq.q: How do I deal with patterns at high speed?
faq.a: Read two obstacles ahead rather than one — at high shaft speeds, reacting to what is immediately in front of you is too slow. Identify the next gap before you reach the current one and begin steering toward it in advance.

faq.q: Does it matter which side I dodge toward?
faq.a: Yes — the leaderboard uses obstacle count as a tiebreaker, so pushing through tight gaps on the correct side (the narrower one) earns more points than the easy route. When distance scores are close, tight-gap threading separates leaderboard positions.

24.title: Entrepreneur Tycoon
24.description: Build a multi-floor business empire from a single coffee stand to a city-spanning retail tower — every product sold pushes you up the leaderboard.
24.fullDescription:
Entrepreneur Tycoon puts you in charge of a vertical business empire. Start with a humble shop on the ground floor, hire staff, stock shelves, and watch customers stream in. Reinvest every dollar to unlock new floors, new product lines, and faster automation.
      Two numbers define your run: total money earned and total products produced. Money is the primary score, but production count is the tiebreaker — so a tycoon who pushes volume always edges out one who only marks up prices.
      Expand from groceries to electronics to a coffee chain. Each new department compounds your income and demands smarter logistics. Upgrade checkout speed, train smarter staff, and automate restocks so the registers never stop ringing.
      The skyline is the limit. How tall will your tower of profit grow?
24.controls: Mouse: Click departments to upgrade, hire staff, restock inventory, and unlock new floors. Touch: Tap any building element to interact.
24.tips: Reinvest aggressively in early floors — compounding income beats hoarding cash. Balance product production with staff capacity; idle shelves earn nothing. Unlock a new floor only after the current one is fully automated, or you'll bottleneck on management. Watch the product counter — it's the tiebreaker that wins close leaderboard races.
24.lore:
They said the city had no room for one more dreamer. You bought the smallest plot on the block anyway, put a single counter on it, and started selling coffee at sunrise.
      One floor became two. Two became a tower. Now your name flickers in neon above the skyline, and rival tycoons watch their charts dip every time your registers chime.
      The empire is yours to build — one customer, one product, one dollar at a time.

faq.q: How do I start the business?
faq.a: You begin with a single ground-floor shop. Click it to open the upgrade menu, stock the shelves, and hire your first staff member. Once customers start arriving and spending, reinvest those earnings into checkout speed to keep the revenue flowing.

faq.q: When should I unlock a new floor?
faq.a: Only unlock a new floor after your current one is fully automated — restocking and staffing running without manual input. Opening a new floor while still managing the previous one manually creates a bottleneck that slows both departments.

faq.q: What is the product count tiebreaker?
faq.a: When multiple players have similar total earnings, the leaderboard ranks by total products produced. A tycoon pushing high product volume at thinner margins can edge out one who only marks up prices, so balance production speed with profitability.

faq.q: What is the most important early upgrade?
faq.a: Reinvest aggressively in early floor income rather than hoarding cash. Compounding income from a well-upgraded first floor funds new departments far faster than gradual investment. Checkout speed and restocking automation are the two highest-return early upgrades.

faq.q: How do product departments differ?
faq.a: Each department — groceries, electronics, coffee, and others — has different price points and customer traffic rates. Higher-value departments like electronics earn more per sale but attract fewer customers; high-volume departments like groceries need faster restocking to maximize throughput.

25.title: Vault of Ashes: Fallen Era
25.description: A grim loadout-driven grid auto-battler — assemble blades, wards, and alchemy across an arcane grid, then watch your build fight on its own through the ruins of a fallen age.
25.fullDescription:
Vault of Ashes: Fallen Era is a loadout-focused grid auto-battler set in a kingdom devoured by an eclipse. You don't control the fight directly — you build it. Slot weapons, armor, potions, and runes onto a tactical grid before each run, then watch your hooded vanguard cut through waves of fallen knights, cinder-wraiths, and gate-born horrors.
      Every cell on the grid matters. Adjacency unlocks synergies: a flame-blade beside an ember rune deals burn ticks; a shield beside a vitality flask trades attack speed for survival. The wrong arrangement loses runs before the first sword swing — the right one shreds bosses in seconds.
      Loot dropped from each chapter expands your vault. Rotate gear between runs, hunt set bonuses, and chase legendary anchor pieces that reshape entire builds. The fallen era doesn't reward reflexes. It rewards preparation.
      The vault is sealed. The eclipse is bleeding. Will your loadout hold the line, or will you join the ash?
25.controls: Mouse Click: Place gear onto grid cells and confirm loadout / Mouse Drag: Rearrange equipped items / Mouse Click (Combat UI): Trigger ultimate abilities and view stats.
25.tips: Adjacency is everything — never place a rune alone if a matching weapon could sit beside it. Save legendary anchor pieces for builds you've already validated in early chapters; rerolling around them mid-run wastes vault slots. When two builds tie on damage, the one with a dedicated potion column survives longer boss phases. Read every set bonus before slotting; one missed two-piece can halve your effective damage.
25.lore:
The eclipse came at midday and never left. Within a single rotation, the kingdom's spires bled fire, the cathedral choirs fell silent, and the Vault — sealed since the first age — cracked at its seam.
      The fallen knights are the ones who answered the bell. They marched into the breach in gleaming order and emerged as something else. Now they patrol the ruins in slow, ceremonial loops, blades dragging across stone.
      You are the last vanguard to remember the sealing rites. Your gear is older than the kingdom that minted it. Each loadout you assemble is half preparation, half remembrance — a wager that the old combinations still hold against what the Vault has become.
25.objectives: Assemble a synergistic loadout of weapons, armor, potions, and runes on a tactical grid before each chapter, leveraging adjacency bonuses and set effects to carry your auto-battling vanguard through escalating waves of fallen knights and gate-born bosses in the ruins of a sealed kingdom.

faq.q: How does the auto-battle actually resolve?
faq.a: Once you confirm a loadout, your vanguard fights waves automatically using the gear, runes, and potions you slotted. Damage, defense, and ability triggers are derived from the grid layout — adjacency between matching pieces produces synergy effects that scale your output far beyond raw item stats.

faq.q: What is grid adjacency and why does it matter?
faq.a: Every gear piece you place on the grid checks its four neighboring cells for matching tags. A flame-blade beside an ember rune adds burn-over-time; a shield beside a vitality flask trades attack speed for survival. Two identical loadouts arranged differently can produce wildly different damage and survival numbers.

faq.q: What are legendary anchor pieces?
faq.a: Anchor pieces are top-tier gear that reshape entire builds. They are rare drops from late chapters and bosses, and they usually demand a specific cluster of supporting gear to function. Save anchors for builds you've already validated in early chapters rather than forcing a run around an unfamiliar piece.

faq.q: Why did my run end so fast?
faq.a: Most early losses come from isolated runes — a rune placed without a matching weapon neighbor contributes almost nothing. Re-check adjacency before confirming, make sure at least one set bonus is active, and dedicate a column to potions if you're losing to drawn-out boss phases.

faq.q: Does the game support mobile?
faq.a: Vault of Ashes: Fallen Era is PC only. The tactical grid requires precise click and drag input for loadout assembly and gear rotation, which the current build does not adapt to touch screens.

26.title: Neon Stack
26.description: A neon timing arcade game — drop glowing blocks onto a rising tower, nail perfect aligns to chain combos, and stack as high as your reflexes allow.
26.fullDescription:
Neon Stack is a one-tap timing game wrapped in a synthwave skyline. A glowing block slides back and forth above your tower — tap to drop it. Land it dead-center and the next block keeps full width; miss, and the overhang shears off, leaving you a narrower platform to aim at.
      Two numbers define your run: total blocks stacked and your best combo streak. Blocks stacked is the primary score, but the leaderboard uses your best combo as the tiebreaker — so a clean run of perfect aligns always outranks a sloppy tower of the same height.
      Every flawless drop tightens the rhythm and feeds your combo multiplier. Break the chain and the tower keeps growing, but your streak resets to zero. The tower never stops rising and the block never stops moving — there is no safe moment, only the next drop.
      Simple to start, brutal to master. How high can you build before one mistimed tap topples the run?
26.controls: Mouse Click / Tap / Spacebar: Drop the moving block onto the stack. Time the release so the block lands flush over the one below — perfect aligns keep full width and build your combo.
26.tips: Watch the block's edge, not its center — your eyes track edges faster and that's where the overhang gets sheared. Find the tower's rhythm and tap on the beat rather than reacting; the speed is constant until you break a combo. A perfect align restores no width, so protect the platform you have — one greedy drop can leave a sliver that ends the run. Best combo is the leaderboard tiebreaker, so chase clean chains even when height feels safe.
26.lore:
Above the synthwave city, the old broadcast tower fell dark decades ago. The signal that built it never stopped transmitting — block by block, frequency by frequency, it still tries to climb back toward the channel it lost.
      Every player who taps in lends the signal a hand. Each clean align is a frequency locked, each combo a verse of the song that once lit the whole skyline. Miss the rhythm and the tower narrows, the neon dims, and the signal starts again.
      No one has reached the top. The leaderboard is just a list of how close the signal got before the rhythm broke.
26.objectives: Drop glowing blocks onto a rising tower with precise timing, landing each one flush over the last to keep full width and chain combo multipliers — maximizing total blocks stacked as your primary score and best combo streak as the leaderboard tiebreaker.

faq.q: How is my score calculated?
faq.a: Total blocks stacked is your primary score — every block you land successfully adds one. Your best combo streak (the longest run of consecutive perfect aligns) is the leaderboard tiebreaker, so when two players reach the same height, the cleaner run with the higher combo ranks above the sloppier one.

faq.q: What counts as a perfect align?
faq.a: Dropping a block so it lands flush over the one below it, with no overhang sheared off. A perfect align keeps the platform at full width and increments your combo multiplier. A partial landing keeps the run alive but cuts the overhang away, narrowing your next target.

faq.q: Why did my tower get so narrow?
faq.a: Each imperfect drop shears off the part of the block hanging past the platform, so the tower can only get narrower, never wider. A string of small misses compounds into a sliver that's nearly impossible to hit — protect your width by aiming for perfect aligns, not just survivable ones.

faq.q: Does the game get faster?
faq.a: The block's sliding speed stays constant through a run — the difficulty comes from the platform narrowing as you miss, not from acceleration. This means the best strategy is to find the steady rhythm early and tap on the beat rather than reacting to each block individually.

faq.q: Does it work on mobile?
faq.a: Yes. Neon Stack is built for both desktop and mobile — tap anywhere on the screen to drop on touch devices, or use a mouse click or the spacebar on desktop. The one-input design plays identically across both.

featuredComments.text: Watch the edge of the block, not the center. Your eyes track edges way faster and the overhang gets sheared from the edge anyway. Switching my focus point doubled my best height in one session.

featuredComments.name: SignalLost
featuredComments.text: An old broadcast tower's signal trying to climb back to the channel it lost, one clean align at a time. That's a lot of atmosphere for a one-tap game and it absolutely lands.

featuredComments.name: ComboChain
featuredComments.text: Best combo is the tiebreaker, so don't get complacent once you're tall. I lost a top-10 spot to someone the same height because my combo was trash. Chase the clean chain even when height feels safe.

featuredComments.name: RhythmTap
featuredComments.text: Stop reacting and start tapping on the beat. The speed is constant, so it's a rhythm game pretending to be a stacking game. Once it clicked I stopped panicking on every block.

featuredComments.name: NarrowLedge
featuredComments.text: One greedy drop leaves you a sliver and the run is basically over. Protect your width like it's the actual score, because narrow platforms kill more runs than tower height ever does.
